what_this_is: Describe a tool and manage this account's live tool-source definitions. Source defaults arrive only from the native task's current source snapshot; source definitions stay in the person's own store, which the caller reads and writes; this tool gives the changes back.

payload.label: Describe a tool
payload.job: Show me one tool's whole row, so I can see how it is written and how to call it
payload.description: Give the tool's id and the rows the Workshop answered (tools:list) as shared. Takes your own saved row of that tool (record type tool, id tool:<tool id>) as saved, read by your AI from your store; it reads no store itself and keeps nothing. Your saved row, unless deleted, replaces the shared row of the same id. Answers the tool's descriptor, who made it (this account or shared), the sample rule of the place it runs (read-only or dry-run samples on a person's own computer, owed until a computer connects), the sample-run checks of your own runnable tool, and the next call to make: save_tool for your own, run_tool for a shared tool that runs, nothing for a screen. A tool there is nothing of to describe answers an error naming find_tool_for_job. It reads one row and changes nothing.

tool_id.description: The id of the tool to describe

shared.description: The rows the Workshop answered: ai-tool-descriptor rows, and tool-placement and tool-licence-class rows when known

saved.description: Your saved row of this tool to use instead of reading it; null when you have none

provenance.source: trillion src/workshop.mjs describeTool (1625-1655) and src/workshop-sample-rules.mjs, moved here; the trillion-rust engine's describe route (GET /work/api/workshop/describe/<id>, src/workshop_describe.rs) deleted when this row took it over

payload.label: Manage my API descriptions
payload.job: List the API descriptions my tools come from, add one for my account, edit it or remove it
payload.description: An empty request lists current default sources and this account's own sources. Change one source with add, edit or remove and keep the same request_key when retrying it. Your source definition stays in this account's original tool-source record; edits keep its added_at and removal keeps a tombstone. Defaults come only from the native task's current source configuration. Source reads still pending are named as pending. Connection fields are references, never keys or tokens. This manages source definitions; it does not sign in to a service, fetch a tool list, or grant permission to execute its tools. An unavailable native source owner refuses without writing.

add.description: A source: id?, kind, https url, name?, nonsecret headers?, connection? {connection_id,field_id}, only?

edit.description: An existing private source id and only the fields to change; null removes optional name, headers, connection or only

remove.description: An active source this account added, by id

request_key.description: Keep this key unchanged when retrying the same change

own.description: The tool-source rows the caller read from the person's own store, as they stand: each {id, value, identity} (id tool-source:<source id>, value the row, identity the store's version of it, read with it). Needed to change or list this account's sources; what is not given is not there.

receipt.description: The tool-source-change row the store holds for this request_key (id from the answer's receipt_id, value {command_identity}), or null when there is none. Give it when retrying the same change, so the change is not made twice.

keep.description: What the run made, for the caller to write where the person keeps it, in one atomic write: rows {id, type, value, expected} (value null removes; expected null means the row must not exist yet, else {identity} is the version it was read at), and the request's tool-source-change receipt {id, type, value, expected: null}. The run itself writes nothing.

provenance.source: ports/source-lifecycle.json retains the original source slices and adaptation boundaries

record_model._what: The original-preserving source definitions and narrow semantic retry receipt. The caller keeps them in the person's own store and gives them back as own and receipt; this tool writes nothing. No secret value is a source field.

payload.label: Read my API descriptions
payload.job: Read the tools my connected API descriptions currently offer
payload.description: Reads the current native-selected source definitions and templates, derives OpenAPI tools, and retains conditional-read/backoff metadata in the current account. A source that is pending, unreadable or needs an unavailable connection is named with that state. Tools are DATA, never privately installed copies. The current native owner supplies and rechecks source/configuration, account and connection authority; request input cannot choose them.

stored.description: What this run reads of the person's own things, read by the caller from where the person keeps them (the engine keeps none) and given here: records: [{id, type, value}] of tool-source (ids starting tool-source:), tool-source-read (ids starting tool-source-read:), as this row's `stored` lists. What is not given is not there.

keep.description: What the run made, for the caller to keep where the person keeps it: rows {id, type, value} (value null removes), settings {label, value}, files {file, base64}. The run itself writes nothing.

provenance.source: Source-first adaptation of the original live source reader, preserving derivation/protocol owners and original source identities; current native supplier and records door replace the retired SQL/runtime.

payload.label: Derive current API description tools
payload.job: Derive the current tools of one native-selected source without opening account records
payload.description: An installed inner source resolver. Native source admission supplies current configuration, original definitions, exact cache snapshots as task DATA and retains their real root/currentness witness through effects and output. Only need and wait are input. Native-only planning derives exact current cache ids through this same owner. The derivation opens no records descriptor, enlarges no caller record rights and writes no durable cache. Credentials remain with the native connection owner.

provenance.source: The same current source derivation owner and protocol DATA as read-my-api-descriptions; this inner row retains native source admission separately from caller record execution rights.
